as_told.title: Salvatore Pais Navy patents
as_told.place_text: Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland

plain: The story concerns Salvatore Pais, a man who filed patents, the legal claims that protect an invention, on behalf of the US Navy in the 2010s. A researcher who goes by the online name UAPGerb, a guest on Jesse Michels's podcast, says Pais was working at Pax River, short for Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy base in Maryland, when he filed them. Michels, the host, tells it again on a later episode and says more about what the patents cover. According to Michels, they deal with inertial mass reduction, meaning making an object act as if it had less mass so it is easier to move, and with high-frequency gravitational waves, meaning fast ripples in gravity. Michels places them around 2018. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would suggest the Navy was officially exploring very unusual ways of moving craft.
